title: Bilateral parking procedures
summary: We introduce the class of bilateral parking procedures on the integer line. While cars try to park in the nearest available spot to their right in the classical case, we consider more general parking rules that allow cars to use the nearest available spot to their left. We show that for a natural subclass of local procedures, the number of corresponding parking functions of length $r$ is always equal to $(r+1)^{r-1}$.
